title: Cross-tool status/prime dashboard
description:
## Problem

Every tool has its own status/prime/orientation command:
- **wai**: `status` + `prime` — project phase, pipeline state, openspec, beads, suggestions
- **dont**: `prime` — claim state, blocking entities
- **fabbro**: `prime` — command/API reference for agents

There's no unified way to get a cross-tool health overview.

## Proposal

Add a `StatusContributor` trait and `StatusBuilder` to genesis:

1. **`StatusContributor` trait** — tools implement:
   - `name() -> &str`
   - `status(repo_root) -> Result<StatusSection>`
   - `suggestions(repo_root) -> Vec<Suggestion>`

2. **`StatusBuilder`** — aggregates registered contributors:
   - `status() -> MultiToolStatus` with sections per tool
   - `suggestions() -> Vec<Suggestion>` — sorted by priority
   - JSON envelope + human output
   - Exit code: healthy=0, warnings>0

## Out of scope (follow-up ticket)

A `SuggestNext` engine that chains status → ranked suggestions is deferred to a follow-up ticket. This issue covers only the `StatusContributor` trait and `StatusBuilder` aggregation.

## Validation

- Tools can register `StatusContributor` impls
- `genesis::status::run()` produces unified output across all registered contributors
- Test: register 2 mock contributors with different status sections, verify aggregated report contains both

## Priority

P0 — pairs with the doctor framework (doctor finds issues, status surfaces them)
close_reason: Status dashboard implemented: StatusContributor trait, StatusBuilder, DoctorStatusBridge, MultiToolStatus with summary and envelope — 26 tests passing, clippy clean, testaruda green

title: Doctor framework: DoctorCheck trait + DoctorRunner CLI
description:
## Problem

Every tool with a `doctor` subcommand writes its own check infrastructure:
- **wai**: Custom `CheckResult`, `DoctorPayload`, `fix_fn` closures — 1,500+ lines across 3 files
- **dont**: Own check system with `--fix` and `--strict` flags
- **pretender**: Custom doctor for config, hooks, plugin health
- **ah**: Custom doctor for adapter detection + `--enable` flag

`genesis::suite_linter` already provides `LintCheck` trait + `LinterRegistry`, but no tool except testaruda uses it. The gap: there's no *doctor CLI pattern* wrapping it.

## Proposal

Extend `suite_linter` into a full doctor framework:

1. **`DoctorCheck` trait** — extends `LintCheck` with:
   - `auto_fixable() -> bool`
   - `fix(&self, repo_root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<LintResult>>`

2. **`DoctorRunner` struct** — orchestrates:
   - `run(repo_root, fix: bool) -> DoctorReport`
   - `run_and_exit(...)` — handles `--fix` flag, JSON vs human output, exit codes, summary
   - `DoctorReport` with pass/warn/fail per check + serializable to envelope

3. **`DoctorRegistry`** that wraps `LinterRegistry` and adds fix capabilities

## Validation

1. Create a mock `DoctorCheck` impl that passes (returns empty results), register it, run `DoctorRunner`, assert pass in the report
2. Create a mock `DoctorCheck` impl that fails (returns error result with a fix), run `DoctorRunner` with `fix: true`, assert the fix was applied
3. All 5 tools (wai, dont, testaruda, pretender, ah) can migrate their doctor to use it
4. `wai doctor --fix` still produces identical output after migration

## Priority

P0 — touches the most tools, eliminates the most duplicated code
close_reason: Doctor framework implemented: DoctorCheck trait, DoctorRunner struct, DoctorReport, CheckEntry, DoctorSummary, CheckStatus — all 33 tests passing, clippy clean, testaruda green

title: Feedback dispatch helper: unified feedback subcommand
description:
## Problem

All 5 Rust tools (dont, wai, testaruda, pretender, ah) implement a `feedback` subcommand that handles `--kind`, `--dry-run`, `--from-last-error`. The `feedback` module already provides scratch, context, redactor, gh — but each tool writes 20–30 lines of CLI dispatch.

## Proposal

Add a single entry point to genesis:

```rust
pub fn handle_feedback(args: FeedbackArgs, tool: &str, version: &str, repo: &str) -> Result<()>
```

Where `FeedbackArgs` bundles:
- `kind: String` (bug|feature|question)
- `dry_run: bool`
- `from_last_error: bool`

## Validation

- Each tool can replace its `Command::Feedback` handler with `genesis::feedback::handle(...)`
- Output is identical (same envelope, same gh invocation, same dry-run behavior)

## Priority

P1 — small effort, eliminates 20–30 lines from 5 tools
close_reason: Unified feedback handler implemented: handle_feedback() with FeedbackArgs, kind validation, typo suggestions, scratch-lookup, context gathering, redaction, gh invocation — 49 tests passing, clippy clean

title: Implement genesis foundation (shared crate for cross-cutting CLI/AIX/self-healing infra)
description:
OpenSpec change: openspec/changes/add-genesis-foundation (validated --strict).

genesis is the shared Rust crate generalizing dont-2j6o. Six modules, each with a named donor: envelope (dont), suggestions (wai), managed_block (wai/dont/espectacular), aix (wai), feedback (new), suite_linter (new). Boundary rule: a module is accepted only if >=2 tools need it; domain logic is never extracted.

Distributed as a git dependency pinned by tag from github.com/charly-vibes/genesis; no crates.io until stable. SemVer; breaking changes require a coordinated tag bump across dependents.

Reference design docs live in this repo's .wai research:
- .wai/projects/genesis-foundation/research/tool-craft.md (suite conventions; Appendix A = compliance matrix)
- .wai/projects/genesis-foundation/research/agent-issue-reporting.md (feedback feature design)

Supersedes dont-2j6o (beads epic, dont repo) — the envelope extraction becomes task 2.1 here; dont-2j6o closes as superseded once task 2.1 lands and its child adoption issues are re-pointed at the per-repo adopt-genesis proposals.

Tasks: openspec/changes/add-genesis-foundation/tasks.md (29 tasks across 8 sections: skeleton, envelope, suggestions, managed_block, feedback, suite_linter, aix, stabilize).

Blocks: every per-repo adopt-genesis / depend-on-genesis proposal (wai, dont, pretender, espectacular, testaruda, crua, livin, vampiro). Those are blocked until genesis tags v0.1.0 (task 8.1).

Acceptance: v0.1.0 tagged with envelope + suggestions + managed_block + aix stable; openspec validate --strict green; dont-2j6o closed as superseded.
notes: EXEC-002 donor sources: clone charly-vibes/dont (src/envelope.rs) and charly-vibes/wai (src/suggestions.rs, src/managed_block.rs) to port from — or work from the charly monorepo where all donors are present. SCOPE-002 split: the 29 tasks mix extract-from-donor (2.x envelope, 3.x suggestions, 4.x managed_block, 7.x aix) with build-new (5.x feedback, 6.x suite_linter). The v0.1.0 tag (task 8.1) gates on the four EXTRACTION modules only; feedback/suite_linter stabilization is a later tag. Verify: openspec validate add-genesis-foundation --strict -> valid; cargo test -p genesis.

title: --version --json pre-parse helper
description:
## Problem

wai and ah both handle `--version --json` before clap parses args (~20 lines each). This pattern is needed because clap's built-in `--version` doesn't participate in the global `--json` flag.

## Proposal

Add to genesis:

```rust
/// Returns true if --version --json was handled and the process should exit.
pub fn maybe_print_version_json(name: &str, version: &str) -> bool
```

Each tool calls it before `Cli::parse()`.

## Validation

- `wai --version --json` still returns the same envelope
- `ah --version --json` still returns the same envelope
- `--version` without `--json` still prints plain text

## Priority

P3 — small effort, eliminates ~20 lines from 2 tools
close_reason: Already implemented as part of the cli module (maybe_print_version_json). Verified: 2 tests passing, returns JSON envelope for --version --json, false otherwise

title: Init scaffolding helpers
description:
## Problem

All 6 Rust tools + fabbro have an `init` command that:
- Creates config from defaults (genesis has `ConfigFile::write()`)
- Creates directory structure
- Sets up `.gitignore` entries
- Installs managed blocks
- (fabbro) Writes agent command files for .claude/, .cursor/

Each tool hardcodes this logic.

## Proposal

Add a `Scaffold` struct with builder pattern:

```rust
let scaffold = Scaffold::new(project_root)
    .dir(".tool/config")
    .dir(".tool/state")
    .default_config(&config)
    .gitignore_entry(".tool/*.tmp")
    .managed_block("TOOL", &content)
    .agent_command_file("tool-command.md", &template)
    .build()?;
```

Returns list of created paths for reporting.

## Validation

1. Test with tempdir: create Scaffold, build it, assert directories exist, config file is valid TOML
2. `wai init` can adopt Scaffold and produce identical directory structure

## Priority

P4 — medium effort, lower urgency than doctor/status
close_reason: Init scaffolding implemented: Scaffold builder with dir/config/gitignore/managed_block/agent_command_file — 11 tests passing, clippy clean, testaruda green
